covers: The two registers of the 8259 interrupt controller

entries.name: IRR, ISR or poll
entries.description: Status port: a read returns the interrupt request register, the in-service register, or the poll result, as the last OCW3 chose.
entries.behaviour: OCW3 bit 0 chooses what a read returns: 0 the interrupt request register, 1 the in-service register with masked bits cleared. After a poll command a read returns 0x80 plus the highest requesting level, or 0 with no request, and ends the poll.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X does not handle the poll command, and its in-service read is not masked by the mask register.

entries.name: command port
entries.description: Command port: takes ICW1, OCW2 or OCW3, told apart by bits 4 and 3 of the byte written.
entries.behaviour: Bit 4 set is ICW1. With bit 4 clear, bit 3 set and bit 7 clear is OCW3, and bits 4 and 3 clear is OCW2. Each is a command entry of this chip.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X takes any byte with bit 4 clear and bit 3 set as OCW3, whatever bit 7 is; MAME needs bit 7 clear.

entries.name: interrupt mask
entries.description: Data port, read: the interrupt mask register, one bit per request line.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the interrupt mask register, with no OCW3 needed. A set bit masks that request line.

entries.name: ICW2-4 or mask
entries.description: Data port, write: the next initialization word after ICW1, and once the sequence is over the interrupt mask.
entries.behaviour: After ICW1 the writes are ICW2 (vector base, low three bits ignored), ICW3 when cascaded and ICW4 when ICW1 asked for it; ICW4 bit 1 is automatic EOI and bit 0 selects 8086 mode. Afterwards each write sets the interrupt mask register.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X logs special fully nested mode and 8085 mode as not handled, and keeps no ICW3 content.
